# Phase-B pilot scoring frame — 15,000 windows, nine metrics + mask fractions

<!-- GENERATED by `python -m dataset.pilot`. Do not hand-edit numbers; re-run to refresh. The per-window CSV is the artifact; this is its cover sheet. -->

Resolves issue #24 (part of the Phase-B map, #23). Builds the window-level frame the whole pruning study (B2/B3) runs on: every window scored on **all nine `dataset.metrics.METRICS` functions at their Gate A3 production resolutions** (#21) plus the three EDM/FLM/WBM mask fractions. Unlike A3's calibration, which scored each metric twice to *measure* the overview, this scores each **once, as production will** — so B2's correlation matrix measures the metrics as they will actually be clustered.

- Windows: **15,000** land-bearing windows (target 15,000) from **115** COGs. Ocean-only windows are skipped; coastal windows are kept (ADR-0001 §3).
- `tpi_proxy` NaN on **4,251** windows (2× box ran off the tile — NaN for that column only, #22).
- Mask columns NaN on **0** windows (a mask was absent/unreadable — surfaced below, never read as 'no edits').
- Provenance: code `dabd6e1-dirty`, snapshot `2026-07-20`, seed `0xdeae`.

## 0. The draw is cell-balanced, not band-balanced (#24, #15)

The frame wraps `dataset.sampling.sample_cogs` with `allocation="proportional"` (**cell-balanced**) and takes *every* land window of each drawn COG, accumulating in the sampler's priority order so any prefix stays band-spread. The distinction that matters — and the one #24 asks to record — is that a **cell** draw and the **window** frame it produces are not the same shape:

- **The COG draw is uniform over cells.** `allocation="proportional"` gives each 1° cell equal probability — the same principle as `prevalence_sample`. By *cell count* the corpus is pole-dense: 55.2% of cells sit above 50° (#15).
- **The window frame is then naturally pixel/area-weighted, not cell-weighted.** Taking every land window means a cell contributes windows in proportion to its pixels, and polar cells hold fewer columns — so the pole-density inversion *discounts itself*. This frame lands at **28.6%** of windows above 50° (§3), close to the corpus's **29.8% by land area** (#15) and far from its 55.2% by cell. That land-area shape is the honest corpus weighting for a window population, and it is exactly what Phase C production will score — every land window of every kept tile.
- **Band-balanced would have gone the wrong way.** The band edges are `(0, 50, 60, 70, 80, 85, 90)` — five of the six bands sit ≥50°, so an equal-per-band draw puts ~83% of its windows above 50°, *more* polar than either the corpus's cell count or its land area. Equal power per band is right for A3's band-*local* artifact hunt (`calibration_sample`); for a representativeness correlation study it is a 5:1 polar distortion, so it is declined here.
